title: DNS over QUIC RFC 9250 Connection Management Architecture
purpose: Define DoQ client connection lifecycle behavior: idle timeout negotiation, connection reuse safety checks, explicit clean close with DOQ_NO_ERROR, and in-progress transaction abandonment on connection failure.
design_summary: The DoqClient connection management slice adds: (1) DoqDefaults.SuggestedIdleTimeout constant and EnsureIdleTimeout helper for negotiating the QUIC idle timeout. (2) DoqClient tracks the last activity timestamp and effective idle timeout; before each query it checks whether idle time is safely below the timeout margin, throwing a clear exception if the connection is too close to expiry. (3) DisposeAsync sends an explicit CONNECTION_CLOSE with DOQ_NO_ERROR before disposing the QUIC connection when there are outstanding queries. (4) An active query counter tracks in-progress transactions; on connection failure all in-progress queries are abandoned and subsequent callers receive a clear ConnectionFailed exception.
data_and_state_considerations: The client adds three fields: a ValueStopwatch or timestamp for idle tracking, an atomic active-query counter, and a failure-indication flag.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The idle timeout check uses a configurable margin; zero margin disables the reuse safety check.
The DOQ_NO_ERROR close in DisposeAsync is best-effort and may fail if the connection is already closed.
In-progress query tracking uses a simple counter; connection failure sets a flag checked by subsequent calls.
risks: Clock skew between client and server can affect idle timeout calculations.
The connection reuse check is advisory (SHOULD level); callers can bypass it by setting IdleTimeoutMargin to zero.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: All changes are confined to DoqDefaults and DoqClient. No changes to DoqServer, DoqStream, or DoqMessageCodec are required.
